source.reason: Mössbauer hyperfine-field parameters (Table 1) and SAXS-based ordered-phase size for the Fe-6.8Al powder sample.

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-6.8Al powder sample the dominant Mössbauer component at B_hf = 30.34 T (Area 45.45%, Vf 44%) cannot be uniquely assigned: it may correspond to the local configuration (7Fe+1Al)nn+(6Fe)nnn or to the Fe3Al DO3 phase ((8Fe)nn+(6Al)nnn), because the two configurations give closely spaced peaks (b0047, b0035).

A low-intensity Mössbauer peak at ~23 T (23.26 T, Area 1.26%, Vf 1.4%) observed for Fe-6.8Al is interpreted as a possible indicator of the presence of Fe3Al phase with a low volume fraction (b0047, Table 1).

SAXS-observed volume fractions of the ordered phase are lower than the DO3 volume fraction obtained by Mössbauer spectroscopy, attributed to the fact that SAXS senses only ordered phase with sharper boundaries whereas Mössbauer traces all local environments including those with diffused boundaries (b0050).

The SAXS ordered-phase diameter/volume-fraction values are presented only in Fig. 4, whose x-axis carries points at 5, 6, 7 and 9 wt% Al (no explicit 6.8 point); the Fe-6.8Al data point appears plotted at ~7 wt% Al, so its exact numerical size (~2.5–3.0 nm) and volume fraction (~0.5–1.0%) are figure-read rather than stated in text (figure_004).

The mechanical properties (yield strength, UTS, elongation, strain-hardening rate), grain/crystallite sizes (25.2, 48.3, 102.3 nm), dislocation density, micro-strain, XRD, SEM and tensile results reported in the paper belong to the 98% cold-rolled and 750 °C (5 min/60 min) annealed BULK Fe-6.8Al samples (a different process), NOT to this 600 °C/60 min powder (Mössbauer/SAXS) sample; they were therefore not attributed to this sample.

The TEM dark-field ordered-phase size of 2.1 ± 0.2 nm for Fe-6.8Al (Fig. 6) is from a bulk TEM specimen (ground and twin-jet electropolished), not explicitly the filed powder used for Mössbauer/SAXS, so it is not attributed to this sample.

All four Fe-Al compositions (Fe-5Al, Fe-6Al, Fe-6.8Al, Fe-9Al) received the same 600 °C/60 min powder annealing treatment; the powder samples were annealed solely to remove the internal stress generated during powder creation by filing (b0016).
